[summary] This document defines the recommended model for assigning usage credits and per-route quotas for Redwood's Hosted API. It covers conversion rules, quota types, enforcement windows, migration steps for existing customers, and examples to ensure predictable cost and predictable capacity for product teams.
[body] Overview:\nThis page describes a prescriptive set of rules and operational procedures for assigning, converting, and enforcing usage credits and per-route quotas for the Redwood Hosted inference product. The goal is to reduce billing surprises for customers while preserving predictable capacity behavior under variable workloads.\n\nWhy this matters:\n- Customers want clear, auditable rules that explain how API calls map to billable units and to runtime capacity quotas.\n- Support and sales need a deterministic conversion matrix when upgrading customers between plans or when granting promotional credits.\n- The platform needs consistent enforcement semantics to avoid noisy neighbor incidents and to honor SLAs for tiered customers.\n\nGoals:\n1) Produce an unambiguous conversion matrix between API actions (generations, embeddings, streaming tokens) and credit consumption.\n2) Define quota types (monthly budget credits, per-minute concurrency, rolling 24h burst allowances) and enforcement windows.\n3) Provide a migration plan for customers on legacy \"token-minute\" pricing to the new credit model.\n4) Provide operational runbook steps for support to troubleshoot quota issues.\n\nNon-goals:\n- This doc does not prescribe enterprise reserved-capacity contracts for Dedicated or Private deployments (covered separately).\n- Not a replacement for the legal Terms — only operational guidance for product and support teams.\n\nCore concepts and definitions:\n- Credit unit (CR): the atomic billing unit for Hosted. All billable operations are expressed in CR.\n- Request-class: {generation, chat, embedding, rerank, classification}. Each class has a per-token and per-request cost profile.\n- Quota bucket: an enforceable allowance attached to an API key or account. Buckets are of three kinds: monthly_budget, concurrency, and burst_pool.\n- Burst pool: a rolling window credit allotment (24h) intended to absorb unexpected traffic spikes without immediate hard-throttling.\n\nConversion matrix (high level):\n| Request-class | Metric consumed | Baseline CR rate | Notes |\n|---------------|-----------------|------------------|-------|\n| Generation | output_tokens + prompt_weighted_input_tokens | 1.0 CR per 1k output tokens + 0.4 CR per 1k input tokens | Streaming prorated per token as emitted |\n| Chat | message_tokens + context_window_amortized | 1.2 CR per 1k tokens | System messages treated as input at 0.4 CR/1k |\n| Embedding | vector_units | 0.25 CR per 1k tokens equivalent | Small fixed cost floor of 0.01 CR to prevent zero-cost queries |\n| Rerank | candidate_eval_units | 0.6 CR per candidate per 1k tokens | Multiply by #candidates |\n\nNote: the matrix above is normative for assigning credits during billing cycles. Quantization and optimized kernels may reduce actual backend resource consumption; platform adjusts cost multipliers quarterly and documents changes in pricing-change-notices.\n\nQuota types and enforcement semantics:\n1) monthly_budget (hard): A monthly CR cap. When exhausted, requests receive HTTP 402 (Payment Required) with body code \"quota_exceeded.monthly_budget\" unless account configured for auto-topup.\n2) concurrency (soft then hard): A per-account concurrent request cap measured over 1s windows. Soft limit issues 429 with header X-Quota-Action: slow-down and offers Retry-After. If soft limit persists for >10s, platform escalates to hard 429 with X-Quota-Blocked.\n3) burst_pool (grace): Rolling 24h pool that replenishes linearly. When monthly_budget is near exhaustion, burst_pool provides allowance up to configured percentage of monthly_budget. Exhausting both results in hard-block.\n\nEnforcement flow (simple):\n1) Request arrives.\n2) Charge estimated CR from burst_pool or monthly_budget based on current state.\n3) If estimated charge exceeds available in both buckets, return block response with suggested remedial steps.\n4) After request completes, reconcile actual CR consumed and adjust buckets; if actual > estimated, reconciliation can result in negative-balance grace (up to 5% of monthly_budget) before hard-block.\n\nMigration story for legacy customers (timeline & steps):\n- Objective: Migrate customers currently on the \"token-minute\" plans to CR model with minimal disruption and clear audit trail.\n- Migration window: Q1 2026 (target).\n- Steps: 1) Export legacy usage logs and compute equivalent CR using the Conversion matrix (generate per-account migration report). 2) Apply one-time migration credit equal to the account's trailing-3-month median monthly consumption + 10% buffer. 3) Flag accounts for manual review if trailing usage shows >3x variance month-to-month. 4) Notify customers 30 days in advance with migration report and sandboxed preview of post-migration invoice.\n\nEdge cases and dispute handling:\n- If a customer disputes the conversion, provide the per-request audit log (request-id, timestamp, tokens_in, tokens_out, estimated_CR, reconciled_CR) for the disputed billing period. Support may apply a refund credit up to 100% for systemic conversion errors discovered by finance.\n- For customers with high variance, recommend Dedicated or reserved capacity rather than extending larger burst pools.\n\nOperational runbook (support-facing quick steps):\n1) When a customer reports \"quota exceeded\":\n   a) Ask for request-id or approximate timestamp and route.\n   b) Check per-account bucket state in Admin Console -> Usage -> Buckets.\n   c) Pull request audit log and reconcile estimated vs actual CR.\n   d) If reconciliation shows a platform bug (e.g., double-counting on retry), escalate to Billing and Runtime teams with label: billing-incident.\n   e) For legitimate overages, offer one-time courtesy credit following the Customer Help Credit policy (max $X for Starter, $Y for Growth).\n2) When a customer needs temporary capacity increase:\n   a) For scheduled events, follow Capacity Ramp procedure: create scheduled uplift in Gateway config, set provisional burst_pool percentage, and create Support ticket with capacity window.\n   b) For emergency spikes, consider temporary auto-topup if account has payment method on file.\n\nMetrics and telemetry to surface:\n- Daily consumed CR per account and per-route.\n- Fraction of requests consuming burst_pool vs month
=== hybrid-fidelity-contract-anchors-and-migration-playbook-2030-01-07
[title] Hybrid Fidelity Contract Anchors and Migration Playbook
[content] summary: >
  This playbook defines product, pricing and technical requirements for "Hybrid Fidelity" commercial bundles (a combined hosted/dedicated/private fidelity contract model), the contract-anchor concept, migration patterns for existing customers, and the operational runbook for rolling out the SKU set. It spans product overview, PRD-style acceptance criteria, design-level integration notes, roadmap milestones, pricing examples and release notes.

## Context and high-level goal

Redwood offers multiple ways to trade cost and latency vs. output fidelity. Customers need clear contract constructs and migration paths when moving between Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments while preserving SLAs and predictable billing. The Hybrid Fidelity Contract Anchors product provides:

- A small set of auditable contract "anchors" that define fidelity bands (Platinum, Gold, Silver) mapped to model families, quantization profiles, and routing policies.
- A migration assistant + billing adapter to transition existing customers onto anchor-based SKUs with minimal invoicing noise.
- A runtime coordination layer (fidelity-orchestrator) that enforces routing, fallback economics, and fidelity fallthrough rules.

Audience: Product managers, commercial leads (GTM), billing/finance, engineering (runtime, billing-bridge, console), customer success.

## Scope

In-scope:
- Definition of fidelity anchors and the canonical SKU mapping.
- PRD acceptance criteria for the migration assistant and billing adapter.
- Design constraints for the fidelity-orchestrator and runtime enforcement hooks.
- Roadmap for a staged roll-out and commercial experiments.

Out-of-scope:
- New model training or model variant creation.
- Deep changes to existing legal contract terms (requires legal team separate engagement).

## Product requirements (PRD style)

Goals:
1. Customers can buy a single contract (anchor) which guarantees a fidelity band across deployments.
2. Transitioning customers must see <= 3% variance on monthly spend (estimate) during migration under typical traffic patterns.
3. Runtime must enforce fidelity contracts with observable fallbacks and per-request auditability.

Key user stories:
- As a Developer, I can select a fidelity anchor on my account and immediately see an estimate of expected latency and monthly cost.
- As an SRE, I can query per-route fidelity decisions and upstream fallback decisions for debugging.
- As a Finance lead, I can reconcile pre- and post-migration invoices using the migration adapter CSV and mapping table.

Acceptance criteria (must pass):
- UI: Console shows anchor selection with estimated 95th percentile latency and monthly spend range.
- API: admin API to set anchor per-tenant returns 200 and an audit entry (event: anchor.changed).
- Billing: Adapter generates mapping file and invoice adjustments for first billing cycle with delta explanation notes.
- Runtime: fidelity-orchestrator logs every cross-variant fallback with reason, matched SLA tag, and cost-delta estimate in telemetry.

## Non-functional requirements

- Latency overhead: fidelity-orchestrator decision path must add < 2ms p50 to request path in hosted mode, < 5ms p50 in private deployments.
- Availability: anchor decision service SLA 99.95% across regions.
- Observability: 100% sampling of anchor change events; 1% sampling of per-request decision traces by default (configurable).

## Design summary (high level)

Components:
- fidelity-orchestrator (service): maps anchor -> runtime policy (preferred model group, allowed quantization levels, routing priority).
- billing-bridge (service): consumes tenant->anchor assignments and emits SKU mapping and billable adjustments.
- console (UI): anchor selector and migration assistant flow.
- migration-assistant (batch + streaming): runs a simulation of expected spend and generates a recommended anchor per tenant.

Key contracts and APIs (examples):
- POST /admin/v1/tenants/{id}/anchor { "anchor": "platinum-v2" } => 200
- GET /admin/v1/tenants/{id}/anchor/logs => list of audit events
- Webhook: /billing/v1/anchor-mappings (billing-bridge) accepts anchor -> sku diff payloads

Runtime enforcement rules (summary):
1. Prefer models in the anchor's whitelist. If capacity unavailable, fallback to anchor-compatible variants following priority list.
2. On fallback, emit telemetry: event.fallback{tenant, route, from_model, to_model, reason, estimated_cost_delta}
3. If fallback leads to > 20% cost delta for the tenant's billing period, trigger an alert to customer-success and billing teams.

Compatibility and limits:
- Anchors are compatible with existing per-route SLOs and can be scoped per-tenant or per-route (tenant-level default with route overrides).
- Migration assistant will warn when historical quantization usage suggests >10% quality risk; those tenants require manual approval.

## Pricing & packaging model

Anchor tiers (canonical):

| Anchor | Model families (preferred) | Typical latency band (p95) | Billing approach |
|--------|----------------------------|----------------------------|------------------|
| Platinum | stateful-opt, large-open | 60–120ms | Higher per-token + fidelity premium, reserved burst capacity included |
| Gold     | balanced-latency, quant-friendly | 80–180ms | Mid per-token with optional reserved pool add-on |
| Silver   | cost-optimized, strong quant | 120–350ms | Lower per-token; preemptible capacity for non-critical workloads |

Pricing rules (examples):
- Base per-token rate derived from model family + quantization multiplier.
- Anchor premium: fixed % uplift for Platinum (e.g., +25%) applied to baseline compute tokens.
- Reserved capacity credits: bundled with Platinum and optionally Gold; redeemed against actual usage.
- Migration credit: first month credit to neutralize invoice delta up to $X or 5% of monthly committed spend (whichever smaller).

Billing edge cases:
- If a tenant is routed to fallback models outside anchor compatibility due to blackout, billing-bridge emits a flagged line item labeled "emergency-fallback" and flags finance reconciliation.

## Migration playbook (step-by-step)

1. Run migration-assistant in simulation mode to profile 30 days of traffic and produce recommended anchor and expected monthly spend delta.
2. Present recommendation to customer via CS portal with toggles: Accept, Request manual review, or Delay.
3. On Accept: schedule a low-risk migration window (24–72h) during low traffic; enable anchor in dry-run (no billing) for 48h and collect telemetry.
4. If dry-run meets quality thresholds (see QA criteria), flip to active anchor and trigger billing adapter for SKU mapping.
5. Monitor first 7-day delta window; if spend delta > 10% or quality regression detected, run rollback steps and open postmortem.

Rollback steps (quick):
1. Disable anchor at tenant level via admin API.
2. Re-apply previous routing policy and

  "space": "customer-success-and-support",
  "author": "Owen Phillips",
  "owner_team": "customer-success",
  "status": "published",
  "created_at": "2026-02-02",
  "last_updated": "2026-02-09",
  "reviewers": [
    "Dev Patel"
  ],
  "labels": [
    "sales",
    "estimates",
    "tokens"
  ],
  "related_pages": [],
  "confidentiality": "internal",
  "body": "## Purpose\nHow solutions engineers estimate a prospect's monthly tokens before a quote. Estimates use an approximate tokenizer and round up 10% for safety. This page is about forecasting before purchase. It does not explain how billed tokens are counted on an invoice; for that, see the token accounting pages and the billing routing page.\n\n## Method\n1. Sample 100 representative requests.\n2. Count characters and divide by 4 for English text.\n3. Multiply by expected monthly volume and add 10%.\n\n_Last reviewed 2026-02-09._"
}

{
  "title": "Usage accounting: retries and streaming cancellation",
  "space": "customer-success-and-support",
  "author": "Aisha Rahman",
  "owner_team": "customer-success",
  "status": "published",
  "created_at": "2025-02-14",
  "last_updated": "2025-02-18",
  "reviewers": [
    "Priya Natarajan",
    "Dev Patel",
    "Ben Carter"
  ],
  "labels": [
    "usage",
    "billing",
    "tokens",
    "streaming",
    "retries",
    "workaround"
  ],
  "confidentiality": "internal",
  "related_pages": [
    "customer-success-and-support/escalation-playbook",
    "eng-platform/runbooks/usage-pipeline"
  ],
  "content": "## Overview\nSome customers reconcile Redwood token usage against internal estimates and may observe higher usage totals. The most common causes are (1) client retries and (2) streaming cancellation behavior.\n\nThis page provides a support-ready explanation and recommended mitigations.\n\n## Key definitions\n- **Attempt**: a single request admitted by the Redwood API gateway (server-side).\n- **Logical request**: what the customer thinks of as one user action; may map to multiple attempts if the client retries.\n\n## What we bill\n### Retries\n- Redwood usage is recorded per-attempt.\n- If a client retries after a timeout or non-200 response, each admitted attempt can be billable.\n- The Usage dashboard lists rows by **request_id** (attempt identifier).\n\n### Streaming cancellation\n- **Prompt tokens** are counted once the request is admitted (even if the client cancels the stream later).\n- **Completion tokens** are counted based on tokens actually generated/streamed prior to cancellation.\n\n## Common customer symptoms\n- We only sent N requests but we see >N rows: retries created additional attempts.\n- We timed out at 15s so we expected zero bill: prompt tokens + partial completion tokens may still be counted.\n\n## Recommended mitigations\n1) Avoid automatic retries on client-side timeouts for long generations.\n2) Increase client timeout where possible (align to max expected generation time).\n3) Reduce max_tokens / output length to meet latency budgets.\n4) For troubleshooting, ask for a small set of request_ids + the customers retry/cancel metrics.\n\n## Support playbook (quick response blurb)\nWe record usage per server-admitted attempt. If your client retries after a timeout, each admitted attempt can appear separately in Usage and can be billable. For streaming, prompt tokens are counted once admitted; completion tokens reflect what was generated before cancellation.\n\n## References\n- SUP-1842 (Northwind AI escalation)\n- INT-330 (UI helper text + KB link)\n- Slack #support thread_ts=1739310605\n"
}

import json,glob,re
kw=re.compile(r'billing|invoice|refund|credit|pricing|price|marketplace|payment|tax|dunning|overage|quota|plan|sla|discount|commit|reseller|partner|usage|token|meter|free|contract|dispute',re.I)
for f in sorted(glob.glob('**/*.json',recursive=True)):
    if f.startswith(('hubspot','github','fireflies')): continue
    d=json.load(open(f))
    if not isinstance(d,dict): continue
    t=d.get('title') or d.get('subject') or d.get('summary') or ''
    if not isinstance(t,str): continue
    st=d.get('status','')
    if kw.search(t) or kw.search(f.split('/')[-1]):
        print(f"{f[:95]:95s} | {str(st)[:12]:12s} | {t[:80]}")
EOF

"""Run workspace agents in a sandbox and exchange JSON messages with the host."""
from __future__ import annotations

import importlib
import json
import os
import sys
import traceback
from enum import StrEnum
from pathlib import Path
from types import ModuleType
from typing import Protocol, TextIO, TypeGuard, runtime_checkable

from .agent_context import (
    ActionInterface,
    AgentBuildContext,
    KitResources,
    ModelConfig,
    ModelGateway,
    activate_agent_context,
)
from .billing import Billing
from .developer import Developer
from .hooks import HookKitBase, ToolRunner
from .jsontypes import Json, JsonObject, is_json_object
from .messages import Message, ToolCall, UserMessage, from_dict, to_dict
from .toolkit import ToolKitBase

RUNTIME_CONFIG = {"company": "Redwood Inference", "role": "billing_support"}
_protocol_out = sys.stdout
_protocol_in = sys.stdin


class HostOp(StrEnum):
    INIT = "init"
    TURN = "turn"
    TOOLS = "tools"


class HostCall(StrEnum):
    MODEL = "model"
    EMBED = "embed"
    BILLING = "billing"
    DEVELOPER = "developer"


@runtime_checkable
class SupportAgent(Protocol):
    def get_init_state(self, *, message_history: list[Message]) -> object: ...

    def generate_next_message(self, message: Message, state: object) -> tuple[Message, object]: ...


@runtime_checkable
class StopsConversation(Protocol):
    def is_stop(self, message: Message) -> bool: ...


class WorkspaceFactory(Protocol):
    def __call__(self) -> object: ...


def _is_factory(value: object) -> TypeGuard[WorkspaceFactory]:
    return callable(value)


def _write(payload: JsonObject) -> None:
    _protocol_out.write(json.dumps(payload) + "\n")
    _protocol_out.flush()


def _read() -> JsonObject:
    line = _protocol_in.readline()
    if not line:
        raise SystemExit(0)
    value = json.loads(line)
    if not is_json_object(value):
        raise TypeError("wire message must be an object")
    return value


def _ask(payload: JsonObject) -> JsonObject:
    _write(payload)
    reply = _read()
    if not reply.get("ok"):
        error = reply.get("error", "host rejected the request")
        raise RuntimeError(str(error))
    return reply


def _factory(module: ModuleType, name: str) -> WorkspaceFactory:
    candidate = module.__dict__.get(name)
    if not _is_factory(candidate):
        raise TypeError(f"workspace module has no callable {name}")
    return candidate


def _load_toolkit() -> ToolKitBase:
    instance = _factory(importlib.import_module("tools"), "Tools")()
    if not isinstance(instance, ToolKitBase):
        raise TypeError("workspace Tools must inherit ToolKitBase")
    return instance


def _load_hooks(root: Path) -> HookKitBase | None:
    if not (root / "hooks.py").is_file():
        return None
    instance = _factory(importlib.import_module("hooks"), "Hooks")()
    if not isinstance(instance, HookKitBase):
        raise TypeError("workspace Hooks must inherit HookKitBase")
    return instance


def _object(value: Json, name: str) -> JsonObject:
    if not is_json_object(value):
        raise TypeError(f"{name} must be an object")
    return value


def _model_config(value: Json) -> ModelConfig:
    data = _object(value, "model configuration")
    model = data.get("model")
    constraints = data.get("constraints", {})
    if not isinstance(model, str) or not is_json_object(constraints):
        raise TypeError("model configuration is invalid")
    return ModelConfig(model, constraints)


def _model_configs(value: Json) -> tuple[ModelConfig, ...]:
    if not isinstance(value, list):
        raise TypeError("model configurations must be a list")
    return tuple(_model_config(item) for item in value)


def _init_gateway(init: JsonObject) -> ModelGateway:
    models = _model_configs(init["models"])
    embeddings = _model_configs(init.get("embedding_models", []))
    return ModelGateway(models, _ask, embeddings)


def _build_agent(root: Path, toolkit: ToolKitBase, gateway: ModelGateway, runner: ToolRunner) -> SupportAgent:
    billing = Billing(_ask)
    toolkit.gateway = gateway
    toolkit.runner = runner
    toolkit.billing = billing
    toolkit.developer = Developer(_ask)
    context = AgentBuildContext(
        action_interface=ActionInterface(tuple(toolkit.get_tools())),
        resources=KitResources.from_root(root),
        model_gateway=gateway,
        runtime_config=RUNTIME_CONFIG,
        billing=billing,
    )
    with activate_agent_context(context):
        agent = _factory(importlib.import_module("agent"), "create_agent")()
    if not isinstance(agent, SupportAgent):
        raise TypeError("workspace agent does not implement the support-agent protocol")
    return agent


def _initial_state(agent: SupportAgent, init: JsonObject) -> object:
    message = from_dict(_object(init["first_message"], "first_message"))
    return agent.get_init_state(message_history=[message])


def _stop(agent: SupportAgent, message: Message) -> bool:
    if isinstance(agent, StopsConversation):
        return bool(agent.is_stop(message))
    return False


def _turn(request: JsonObject, agent: SupportAgent, runner: ToolRunner, state: object) -> tuple[JsonObject, object]:
    message = from_dict(_object(request["message"], "message"))
    if isinstance(message, UserMessage):
        message.content = runner.user_message(message.content or "")
    response, new_state = agent.generate_next_message(message, state)
    return {"ok": True, "message": to_dict(response), "stop": _stop(agent, response)}, new_state


def _tool_calls(value: Json) -> list[ToolCall]:
    if not isinstance(value, list):
        raise TypeError("tool_calls must be a list")
    calls: list[ToolCall] = []
    for item in value:
        data = _object(item, "tool call")
        call_id = data.get("id")
        name = data.get("name")
        arguments = data.get("arguments", {})
        if not isinstance(call_id, str) or not isinstance(name, str) or not is_json_object(arguments):
            raise TypeError("tool call is invalid")
        calls.append(ToolCall(call_id, name, arguments))
    return calls


def _tools(request: JsonObject, runner: ToolRunner) -> JsonObject:
    calls = _tool_calls(request["tool_calls"])
    return {"ok": True, "tool_messages": [to_dict(runner.run(call)) for call in calls]}


def _handle_request(
    request: JsonObject,
    agent: SupportAgent,
    runner: ToolRunner,
    state: object,
) -> tuple[JsonObject | None, object]:
    operation = request.get("op")
    if operation == HostOp.TURN:
        response, new_state = _turn(request, agent, runner, state)
        return response, new_state
    if operation == HostOp.TOOLS:
        return _tools(request, runner), state
    return None, state


def _serve(agent: SupportAgent, runner: ToolRunner, state: object) -> None:
    while True:
        request = _read()
        try:
            response, state = _handle_request(request, agent, runner, state)
            if response is None:
                return
            _write(response)
        except Exception:
            _write({"ok": False, "error": traceback.format_exc(limit=8)})


def _redirect_stdio(null_input: TextIO) -> None:
    global _protocol_out, _protocol_in
    _protocol_out, _protocol_in = sys.stdout, sys.stdin
    sys.stdout, sys.stdin = sys.stderr, null_input


def _run_candidate() -> None:
    init = _read()
    root = Path.cwd()
    sys.path.insert(0, str(root))
    toolkit = _load_toolkit()
    runner = ToolRunner(toolkit, _load_hooks(root))
    gateway = _init_gateway(init)
    agent = _build_agent(root, toolkit, gateway, runner)
    state = _initial_state(agent, init)
    _write({"ok": True})
    _serve(agent, runner, state)


def main() -> None:
    with open(os.devnull) as null_input:
        _redirect_stdio(null_input)
        _run_candidate()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
"""The host side of one support conversation: the agent process, its sandbox copy, and the turn loop.

Grading and practice conversations (`redwood_kit.practice`) both run through this module, so a practice
conversation drives the agent exactly as a graded one does: the same greeting, wire protocol, tool
rounds, step limit, resource limits and endings. Only the services behind the agent's calls differ,
and a session supplies them through `serve`.

`AgentProcess` owns the subprocess running `redwood_kit.candidate` and answers its `model`, `embed`,
`billing` and `developer` calls. `Session` plays one conversation: the greeting, agent turns with tool
rounds, and the developer's replies, until the developer ends it, the agent stops itself, or the
conversation reaches `MAX_STEPS`.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import contextlib
import glob
import json
import os
import pwd
import shutil
import signal
import stat
import subprocess
import sys
import threading
from collections.abc import Callable
from dataclasses import asdict, dataclass
from enum import StrEnum
from pathlib import Path

from pydantic import BaseModel, ConfigDict, TypeAdapter

from .agent_context import ModelConfig
from .customer import OUT_OF_SCOPE_TOKEN, STOP_TOKENS, TRANSFER_TOKEN, Speaker
from .jsontypes import Json, JsonObject
from .messages import AssistantMessage, Message, MultiToolMessage, ToolMessage, UserMessage, from_dict, to_dict

GREETING = "Hi! How can I help you today?"
MAX_STEPS = 40  # agent turns, including tool rounds, per conversation
CALL_TIMEOUT = 180
KIT_PATH = "/opt"
MODEL_KWARGS = {"max_output_tokens"}  # the only argument an agent may pass with a model call
EMBED_KWARGS: set[str] = set()

# One thread per library: RLIMIT_NPROC counts threads across every process of the agent's user.
THREADS = {name: "1" for name in (
    "OMP_NUM_THREADS", "OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS", "MKL_NUM_THREADS",
    "NUMEXPR_NUM_THREADS", "RAYON_NUM_THREADS", "POLARS_MAX_THREADS",
)}

# Run by the child itself before any workspace code: preexec_fn is unsafe once conversations run in
# threads, and an unprivileged process cannot raise a hard limit back up. A hard limit already lower than
# the cap is kept (an unprivileged practice run could not raise it; the root grader never meets one).
LIMITS = (
    "import resource\n"
    "for limit, value in ((resource.RLIMIT_NPROC, 1024), (resource.RLIMIT_FSIZE, 128 << 20),\n"
    "                     (resource.RLIMIT_AS, 4 << 30), (resource.RLIMIT_CORE, 0)):\n"
    "    hard = resource.getrlimit(limit)[1]\n"
    "    value = value if hard == resource.RLIM_INFINITY else min(value, hard)\n"
    "    resource.setrlimit(limit, (value, value))\n"
)

_JSON_OBJECT: TypeAdapter[JsonObject] = TypeAdapter(JsonObject)


class Termination(StrEnum):
    """How a conversation ended; `finished` splits a real ending from a run that died early."""

    CUSTOMER_STOP = "customer_stop"
    CUSTOMER_TRANSFER = "customer_transfer"
    CUSTOMER_OUT_OF_SCOPE = "customer_out_of_scope"
    AGENT_STOP = "agent_stop"
    MAX_STEPS = "max_steps"
    AGENT_ERROR = "agent_error"

    @property
    def finished(self) -> bool:
        return self not in {Termination.MAX_STEPS, Termination.AGENT_ERROR}


class ModelRequest(BaseModel):
    """A `call:"model"` wire request from the agent, re-validated before serving."""

    model_config = ConfigDict(frozen=True, extra="forbid")

    model: str
    messages: list[JsonObject] = []
    tools: list[JsonObject] | None = None
    tool_choice: Json = None
    kwargs: JsonObject = {}


class EmbedRequest(BaseModel):
    """A `call:"embed"` wire request from the agent."""

    model_config = ConfigDict(frozen=True, extra="forbid")

    model: str
    inputs: str | list[str] = []  # a bare string is refused by checked_inputs with its own message
    kwargs: JsonObject = {}


class TurnReply(BaseModel):
    """The agent's answer to `op: turn`: its message and whether it ends the conversation."""

    message: JsonObject
    stop: bool = False


class ToolsReply(BaseModel):
    """The agent's answer to `op: tools`: one tool message per call, in call order."""

    tool_messages: list[JsonObject]


def wire_payload(reply: JsonObject) -> JsonObject:
    return {key: value for key, value in reply.items() if key != "call"}


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- the sandbox copy


def freeze(workspace: Path, destination: Path) -> None:
    """Copy the workspace to a read-only tree with no links or set-id bits (root-owned when run as root)."""
    if destination.exists():
        _unlock(destination)
        shutil.rmtree(destination)
    shutil.copytree(workspace, destination, symlinks=True, ignore=shutil.ignore_patterns("__pycache__", "*.pyc"))
    entries = [destination, *destination.rglob("*")]
    for path in entries:
        _check_safe_entry(path, destination)
    for path in reversed(entries):
        _lock(path)
    for required in ("agent.py", "tools.py"):
        if not (destination / required).is_file():
            raise ValueError(f"workspace/{required} is missing")


def unlock(destination: Path) -> None:
    """Make a frozen tree removable again by its owner."""
    _unlock(destination)


def _unlock(destination: Path) -> None:
    for path in (destination, *destination.rglob("*")):
        if path.is_dir():
            path.chmod(0o700)


def _check_safe_entry(path: Path, destination: Path) -> None:
    relative = path.relative_to(destination)
    if path.is_symlink() or not (path.is_dir() or path.is_file()):
        raise ValueError(f"workspace contains a link or special file: {relative}")
    if path.stat().st_mode & (stat.S_ISUID | stat.S_ISGID):
        raise ValueError(f"workspace contains set-ID bits: {relative}")


def _lock(path: Path) -> None:
    if os.geteuid() == 0:
        os.chown(path, 0, 0)
    path.chmod(0o555 if path.is_dir() or path.stat().st_mode & 0o111 else 0o444)


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- the agent process


Serve = Callable[[JsonObject], JsonObject]


FAKETIME_LIBRARY = "/usr/lib/*/faketime/libfaketime.so.1"


def clock_env(clock: str) -> dict[str, str]:
    """Environment that starts the agent's clock at `clock` ("YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS", UTC) and lets it run forward.

    The conversations happen on their own dates, not the host's, so an agent that reads the time (datetime.now(),
    date.today()) sees the conversation's. Needs libfaketime, which the image installs; on Linux without it the
    run stops rather than give the agent the wrong date. Elsewhere (local tests on macOS) the host clock stays.
    """
    if not clock:
        return {}
    found = sorted(glob.glob(FAKETIME_LIBRARY))
    if not found:
        if sys.platform == "linux":
            raise RuntimeError(f"libfaketime not found at {FAKETIME_LIBRARY}: cannot set the agent's clock")
        return {}
    return {"LD_PRELOAD": found[0], "FAKETIME": f"@{clock}", "FAKETIME_DONT_FAKE_MONOTONIC": "1", "TZ": "UTC"}


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Sandbox:
    """How the agent process runs: as `user` when the host is root, with `limits` on its resources, importing the
    kit from `kit_path`, its clock starting at `clock` (empty: the host's). Errors of a `passthrough` type mean the
    run itself failed and propagate."""

    user: pwd.struct_passwd | None = None
    limits: bool = True
    kit_path: str = KIT_PATH
    passthrough: tuple[type[BaseException], ...] = ()
    clock: str = ""


class AgentProcess:
    """The subprocess running redwood_kit.candidate from a frozen workspace.

    `serve` answers each call the agent makes (`model`, `embed`, `billing`, `developer`) with the reply
    body; an exception becomes an `ok: false` reply the agent sees, except the sandbox's passthrough types.
    """

    def __init__(self, workspace: Path, log: Path, home: Path, serve: Serve, sandbox: Sandbox) -> None:
        self.serve = serve
        self.passthrough = sandbox.passthrough
        self.position = 0  # set by the session: the position of the current request in the conversation
        self.log = log.open("a")
        user = sandbox.user
        start = f"import sys; sys.path.insert(0, {sandbox.kit_path!r}); from redwood_kit.candidate import main; main()"
        self.process = subprocess.Popen(
            [sys.executable, "-I", "-B", "-c", (LIMITS if sandbox.limits else "") + start],
            cwd=workspace,
            env={"HOME": str(home), "TMPDIR": str(home), "LANG": "C.UTF-8", "PATH": "/usr/local/bin:/usr/bin:/bin",
                 **THREADS, **clock_env(sandbox.clock)},
            stdin=subprocess.PIPE, stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=self.log,
            text=True, bufsize=1, start_new_session=True,
            user=user.pw_uid if user else None, group=user.pw_gid if user else None,
            extra_groups=() if user else None,
        )

    def close(self) -> None:
        with contextlib.suppress(ProcessLookupError, PermissionError):  # macOS: EPERM for an exited group
            os.killpg(self.process.pid, signal.SIGKILL)
        self.process.wait(timeout=10)
        self.log.close()

    def _write(self, payload: JsonObject) -> None:
        assert self.process.stdin is not None
        self.process.stdin.write(json.dumps(payload) + "\n")
        self.process.stdin.flush()

    def _read(self) -> JsonObject:
        timer = threading.Timer(CALL_TIMEOUT, lambda: os.killpg(self.process.pid, signal.SIGKILL))
        timer.start()
        try:
            assert self.process.stdout is not None
            line = self.process.stdout.readline()
        finally:
            timer.cancel()
        if not line:
            raise RuntimeError("candidate process exited or timed out")
        return _JSON_OBJECT.validate_json(line)

    def request(self, payload: JsonObject) -> JsonObject:
        """Send one request and serve the agent's calls until its reply arrives."""
        self._write(payload)
        while (reply := self._read()).get("call"):
            try:
                self._write({"ok": True, **self.serve(reply)})
            except self.passthrough:
                raise  # not the agent's doing: the run is invalid
            except Exception as error:
                self._write({"ok": False, "error": str(error)[:2000]})
        if not reply.get("ok"):
            raise RuntimeError(f"candidate error: {reply.get('error')}")
        return reply


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- the conversation


def _stopped(message: Message) -> bool:
    return isinstance(message, UserMessage) and any(token in (message.content or "") for token in STOP_TOKENS)


_CUSTOMER_ENDINGS = (
    (TRANSFER_TOKEN, Termination.CUSTOMER_TRANSFER),
    (OUT_OF_SCOPE_TOKEN, Termination.CUSTOMER_OUT_OF_SCOPE),
)


def _customer_termination(message: Message) -> Termination:
    text = "" if isinstance(message, MultiToolMessage) else message.content or ""
    return next((ending for token, ending in _CUSTOMER_ENDINGS if token in text), Termination.CUSTOMER_STOP)


def _tool_message(item: JsonObject) -> ToolMessage:
    message = from_dict(item)
    if not isinstance(message, ToolMessage):
        raise TypeError("expected a tool message")
    return message


class Session:
    """One conversation: greeting, agent turns with tool rounds, and the developer's replies.

    A subclass supplies the agent process (`start`), the models it may call, and whether the
    conversation has been handed to a team. `run` ends when the developer sends a stop token, the
    agent stops itself, or the conversation hits `MAX_STEPS`; an error of a `passthrough` type
    propagates (an invalid run), any other becomes `agent_error`.
    """

    passthrough: tuple[type[BaseException], ...] = ()

    def __init__(self, customer: Speaker) -> None:
        self.customer = customer
        self.max_steps = MAX_STEPS
        self.messages: list[Message] = [AssistantMessage(content=GREETING)]
        self.agent: AgentProcess | None = None
        self.termination = Termination.AGENT_ERROR
        self.reply: str | None = None  # the agent's last text reply
        self.error: str | None = None

    # ---- supplied by a subclass

    def start(self) -> AgentProcess:
        raise NotImplementedError

    def models(self) -> tuple[tuple[ModelConfig, ...], tuple[ModelConfig, ...]]:
        """(agent models, embedding models) the agent is told it may call."""
        raise NotImplementedError

    def handed_off(self) -> bool:
        raise NotImplementedError

    # ---- the loop

    def run(self) -> None:
        try:
            self._converse()
        except self.passthrough:
            raise
        except Exception as error:
            self.termination = Termination.AGENT_ERROR
            self.error = f"{type(error).__name__}: {error}"[:4000]

    def _converse(self) -> None:
        pending = self._open()
        steps = 0
        while not _stopped(pending):
            if steps == self.max_steps:
                self.termination = Termination.MAX_STEPS
                return
            steps += 1
            customer_message = self._turn(pending)
            if customer_message is None:
                return  # the agent stopped itself
            pending = customer_message
        self.termination = _customer_termination(pending)

    def _open(self) -> Message:
        self.agent = self.start()
        models, embedding_models = self.models()
        self.agent.request({"op": "init", "models": [asdict(m) for m in models],
                            "embedding_models": [asdict(m) for m in embedding_models],
                            "first_message": to_dict(self.messages[0])})
        pending = self.customer.reply(GREETING, handed_off=False)
        self.messages.append(pending)
        return pending

    def _turn(self, pending: Message) -> Message | None:
        """One agent turn plus any tool rounds; returns the next developer message, or None on agent stop."""
        agent = self._agent()
        agent.position = len(self.messages)
        turn = TurnReply.model_validate(agent.request({"op": "turn", "message": to_dict(pending)}))
        reply = from_dict(turn.message)
        self.messages.append(reply)
        if not isinstance(reply, AssistantMessage) or reply.has_text_content() == reply.is_tool_call():
            raise RuntimeError("agent returned a message that is neither text nor tool calls")
        next_pending = self._run_tool_calls(reply) if reply.is_tool_call() else None
        if not reply.is_tool_call():
            self.reply = reply.content
        if turn.stop:  # after any tool calls on the closing message have run
            self.termination = Termination.AGENT_STOP
            return None
        if next_pending is not None:
            return next_pending
        answer = self.customer.reply(reply.content or "", handed_off=self.handed_off())
        self.messages.append(answer)
        return answer

    def _run_tool_calls(self, reply: AssistantMessage) -> Message:
        agent = self._agent()
        agent.position = len(self.messages)
        outputs = ToolsReply.model_validate(
            agent.request({"op": "tools", "tool_calls": [asdict(c) for c in reply.tool_calls or []]}))
        tool_messages = [_tool_message(item) for item in outputs.tool_messages]
        self.messages.extend(tool_messages)
        return tool_messages[0] if len(tool_messages) == 1 else MultiToolMessage(tool_messages)

    def _agent(self) -> AgentProcess:
        if self.agent is None:
            raise RuntimeError("conversation has no agent process")
        return self.agent

"""Run workspace agents in a sandbox and exchange JSON messages with the host."""
from __future__ import annotations

import importlib
import json
import os
import sys
import traceback
from enum import StrEnum
from pathlib import Path
from types import ModuleType
from typing import Protocol, TextIO, TypeGuard, runtime_checkable

from .agent_context import (
    ActionInterface,
    AgentBuildContext,
    KitResources,
    ModelConfig,
    ModelGateway,
    activate_agent_context,
)
from .billing import Billing
from .developer import Developer
from .hooks import HookKitBase, ToolRunner
from .jsontypes import Json, JsonObject, is_json_object
from .messages import Message, ToolCall, UserMessage, from_dict, to_dict
from .toolkit import ToolKitBase

RUNTIME_CONFIG = {"company": "Redwood Inference", "role": "billing_support"}
_protocol_out = sys.stdout
_protocol_in = sys.stdin


class HostOp(StrEnum):
    INIT = "init"
    TURN = "turn"
    TOOLS = "tools"


class HostCall(StrEnum):
    MODEL = "model"
    EMBED = "embed"
    BILLING = "billing"
    DEVELOPER = "developer"


@runtime_checkable
class SupportAgent(Protocol):
    def get_init_state(self, *, message_history: list[Message]) -> object: ...

    def generate_next_message(self, message: Message, state: object) -> tuple[Message, object]: ...


@runtime_checkable
class StopsConversation(Protocol):
    def is_stop(self, message: Message) -> bool: ...


class WorkspaceFactory(Protocol):
    def __call__(self) -> object: ...


def _is_factory(value: object) -> TypeGuard[WorkspaceFactory]:
    return callable(value)


def _write(payload: JsonObject) -> None:
    _protocol_out.write(json.dumps(payload) + "\n")
    _protocol_out.flush()


def _read() -> JsonObject:
    line = _protocol_in.readline()
    if not line:
        raise SystemExit(0)
    value = json.loads(line)
    if not is_json_object(value):
        raise TypeError("wire message must be an object")
    return value


def _ask(payload: JsonObject) -> JsonObject:
    _write(payload)
    reply = _read()
    if not reply.get("ok"):
        error = reply.get("error", "host rejected the request")
        raise RuntimeError(str(error))
    return reply


def _factory(module: ModuleType, name: str) -> WorkspaceFactory:
    candidate = module.__dict__.get(name)
    if not _is_factory(candidate):
        raise TypeError(f"workspace module has no callable {name}")
    return candidate


def _load_toolkit() -> ToolKitBase:
    instance = _factory(importlib.import_module("tools"), "Tools")()
    if not isinstance(instance, ToolKitBase):
        raise TypeError("workspace Tools must inherit ToolKitBase")
    return instance


def _load_hooks(root: Path) -> HookKitBase | None:
    if not (root / "hooks.py").is_file():
        return None
    instance = _factory(importlib.import_module("hooks"), "Hooks")()
    if not isinstance(instance, HookKitBase):
        raise TypeError("workspace Hooks must inherit HookKitBase")
    return instance


def _object(value: Json, name: str) -> JsonObject:
    if not is_json_object(value):
        raise TypeError(f"{name} must be an object")
    return value


def _model_config(value: Json) -> ModelConfig:
    data = _object(value, "model configuration")
    model = data.get("model")
    constraints = data.get("constraints", {})
    if not isinstance(model, str) or not is_json_object(constraints):
        raise TypeError("model configuration is invalid")
    return ModelConfig(model, constraints)


def _model_configs(value: Json) -> tuple[ModelConfig, ...]:
    if not isinstance(value, list):
        raise TypeError("model configurations must be a list")
    return tuple(_model_config(item) for item in value)


def _init_gateway(init: JsonObject) -> ModelGateway:
    models = _model_configs(init["models"])
    embeddings = _model_configs(init.get("embedding_models", []))
    return ModelGateway(models, _ask, embeddings)


def _build_agent(root: Path, toolkit: ToolKitBase, gateway: ModelGateway, runner: ToolRunner) -> SupportAgent:
    billing = Billing(_ask)
    toolkit.gateway = gateway
    toolkit.runner = runner
    toolkit.billing = billing
    toolkit.developer = Developer(_ask)
    context = AgentBuildContext(
        action_interface=ActionInterface(tuple(toolkit.get_tools())),
        resources=KitResources.from_root(root),
        model_gateway=gateway,
        runtime_config=RUNTIME_CONFIG,
        billing=billing,
    )
    with activate_agent_context(context):
        agent = _factory(importlib.import_module("agent"), "create_agent")()
    if not isinstance(agent, SupportAgent):
        raise TypeError("workspace agent does not implement the support-agent protocol")
    return agent


def _initial_state(agent: SupportAgent, init: JsonObject) -> object:
    message = from_dict(_object(init["first_message"], "first_message"))
    return agent.get_init_state(message_history=[message])


def _stop(agent: SupportAgent, message: Message) -> bool:
    if isinstance(agent, StopsConversation):
        return bool(agent.is_stop(message))
    return False


def _turn(request: JsonObject, agent: SupportAgent, runner: ToolRunner, state: object) -> tuple[JsonObject, object]:
    message = from_dict(_object(request["message"], "message"))
    if isinstance(message, UserMessage):
        message.content = runner.user_message(message.content or "")
    response, new_state = agent.generate_next_message(message, state)
    return {"ok": True, "message": to_dict(response), "stop": _stop(agent, response)}, new_state


def _tool_calls(value: Json) -> list[ToolCall]:
    if not isinstance(value, list):
        raise TypeError("tool_calls must be a list")
    calls: list[ToolCall] = []
    for item in value:
        data = _object(item, "tool call")
        call_id = data.get("id")
        name = data.get("name")
        arguments = data.get("arguments", {})
        if not isinstance(call_id, str) or not isinstance(name, str) or not is_json_object(arguments):
            raise TypeError("tool call is invalid")
        calls.append(ToolCall(call_id, name, arguments))
    return calls


def _tools(request: JsonObject, runner: ToolRunner) -> JsonObject:
    calls = _tool_calls(request["tool_calls"])
    return {"ok": True, "tool_messages": [to_dict(runner.run(call)) for call in calls]}


def _handle_request(
    request: JsonObject,
    agent: SupportAgent,
    runner: ToolRunner,
    state: object,
) -> tuple[JsonObject | None, object]:
    operation = request.get("op")
    if operation == HostOp.TURN:
        response, new_state = _turn(request, agent, runner, state)
        return response, new_state
    if operation == HostOp.TOOLS:
        return _tools(request, runner), state
    return None, state


def _serve(agent: SupportAgent, runner: ToolRunner, state: object) -> None:
    while True:
        request = _read()
        try:
            response, state = _handle_request(request, agent, runner, state)
            if response is None:
                return
            _write(response)
        except Exception:
            _write({"ok": False, "error": traceback.format_exc(limit=8)})


def _redirect_stdio(null_input: TextIO) -> None:
    global _protocol_out, _protocol_in
    _protocol_out, _protocol_in = sys.stdout, sys.stdin
    sys.stdout, sys.stdin = sys.stderr, null_input


def _run_candidate() -> None:
    init = _read()
    root = Path.cwd()
    sys.path.insert(0, str(root))
    toolkit = _load_toolkit()
    runner = ToolRunner(toolkit, _load_hooks(root))
    gateway = _init_gateway(init)
    agent = _build_agent(root, toolkit, gateway, runner)
    state = _initial_state(agent, init)
    _write({"ok": True})
    _serve(agent, runner, state)


def main() -> None:
    with open(os.devnull) as null_input:
        _redirect_stdio(null_input)
        _run_candidate()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
"""The host side of one support conversation: the agent process, its sandbox copy, and the turn loop.

Grading and practice conversations (`redwood_kit.practice`) both run through this module, so a practice
conversation drives the agent exactly as a graded one does: the same greeting, wire protocol, tool
rounds, step limit, resource limits and endings. Only the services behind the agent's calls differ,
and a session supplies them through `serve`.

`AgentProcess` owns the subprocess running `redwood_kit.candidate` and answers its `model`, `embed`,
`billing` and `developer` calls. `Session` plays one conversation: the greeting, agent turns with tool
rounds, and the developer's replies, until the developer ends it, the agent stops itself, or the
conversation reaches `MAX_STEPS`.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import contextlib
import glob
import json
import os
import pwd
import shutil
import signal
import stat
import subprocess
import sys
import threading
from collections.abc import Callable
from dataclasses import asdict, dataclass
from enum import StrEnum
from pathlib import Path

from pydantic import BaseModel, ConfigDict, TypeAdapter

from .agent_context import ModelConfig
from .customer import OUT_OF_SCOPE_TOKEN, STOP_TOKENS, TRANSFER_TOKEN, Speaker
from .jsontypes import Json, JsonObject
from .messages import AssistantMessage, Message, MultiToolMessage, ToolMessage, UserMessage, from_dict, to_dict

GREETING = "Hi! How can I help you today?"
MAX_STEPS = 40  # agent turns, including tool rounds, per conversation
CALL_TIMEOUT = 180
KIT_PATH = "/opt"
MODEL_KWARGS = {"max_output_tokens"}  # the only argument an agent may pass with a model call
EMBED_KWARGS: set[str] = set()

# One thread per library: RLIMIT_NPROC counts threads across every process of the agent's user.
THREADS = {name: "1" for name in (
    "OMP_NUM_THREADS", "OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS", "MKL_NUM_THREADS",
    "NUMEXPR_NUM_THREADS", "RAYON_NUM_THREADS", "POLARS_MAX_THREADS",
)}

# Run by the child itself before any workspace code: preexec_fn is unsafe once conversations run in
# threads, and an unprivileged process cannot raise a hard limit back up. A hard limit already lower than
# the cap is kept (an unprivileged practice run could not raise it; the root grader never meets one).
LIMITS = (
    "import resource\n"
    "for limit, value in ((resource.RLIMIT_NPROC, 1024), (resource.RLIMIT_FSIZE, 128 << 20),\n"
    "                     (resource.RLIMIT_AS, 4 << 30), (resource.RLIMIT_CORE, 0)):\n"
    "    hard = resource.getrlimit(limit)[1]\n"
    "    value = value if hard == resource.RLIM_INFINITY else min(value, hard)\n"
    "    resource.setrlimit(limit, (value, value))\n"
)

_JSON_OBJECT: TypeAdapter[JsonObject] = TypeAdapter(JsonObject)


class Termination(StrEnum):
    """How a conversation ended; `finished` splits a real ending from a run that died early."""

    CUSTOMER_STOP = "customer_stop"
    CUSTOMER_TRANSFER = "customer_transfer"
    CUSTOMER_OUT_OF_SCOPE = "customer_out_of_scope"
    AGENT_STOP = "agent_stop"
    MAX_STEPS = "max_steps"
    AGENT_ERROR = "agent_error"

    @property
    def finished(self) -> bool:
        return self not in {Termination.MAX_STEPS, Termination.AGENT_ERROR}


class ModelRequest(BaseModel):
    """A `call:"model"` wire request from the agent, re-validated before serving."""

    model_config = ConfigDict(frozen=True, extra="forbid")

    model: str
    messages: list[JsonObject] = []
    tools: list[JsonObject] | None = None
    tool_choice: Json = None
    kwargs: JsonObject = {}


class EmbedRequest(BaseModel):
    """A `call:"embed"` wire request from the agent."""

    model_config = ConfigDict(frozen=True, extra="forbid")

    model: str
    inputs: str | list[str] = []  # a bare string is refused by checked_inputs with its own message
    kwargs: JsonObject = {}


class TurnReply(BaseModel):
    """The agent's answer to `op: turn`: its message and whether it ends the conversation."""

    message: JsonObject
    stop: bool = False


class ToolsReply(BaseModel):
    """The agent's answer to `op: tools`: one tool message per call, in call order."""

    tool_messages: list[JsonObject]


def wire_payload(reply: JsonObject) -> JsonObject:
    return {key: value for key, value in reply.items() if key != "call"}


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- the sandbox copy


def freeze(workspace: Path, destination: Path) -> None:
    """Copy the workspace to a read-only tree with no links or set-id bits (root-owned when run as root)."""
    if destination.exists():
        _unlock(destination)
        shutil.rmtree(destination)
    shutil.copytree(workspace, destination, symlinks=True, ignore=shutil.ignore_patterns("__pycache__", "*.pyc"))
    entries = [destination, *destination.rglob("*")]
    for path in entries:
        _check_safe_entry(path, destination)
    for path in reversed(entries):
        _lock(path)
    for required in ("agent.py", "tools.py"):
        if not (destination / required).is_file():
            raise ValueError(f"workspace/{required} is missing")


def unlock(destination: Path) -> None:
    """Make a frozen tree removable again by its owner."""
    _unlock(destination)


def _unlock(destination: Path) -> None:
    for path in (destination, *destination.rglob("*")):
        if path.is_dir():
            path.chmod(0o700)


def _check_safe_entry(path: Path, destination: Path) -> None:
    relative = path.relative_to(destination)
    if path.is_symlink() or not (path.is_dir() or path.is_file()):
        raise ValueError(f"workspace contains a link or special file: {relative}")
    if path.stat().st_mode & (stat.S_ISUID | stat.S_ISGID):
        raise ValueError(f"workspace contains set-ID bits: {relative}")


def _lock(path: Path) -> None:
    if os.geteuid() == 0:
        os.chown(path, 0, 0)
    path.chmod(0o555 if path.is_dir() or path.stat().st_mode & 0o111 else 0o444)


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- the agent process


Serve = Callable[[JsonObject], JsonObject]


FAKETIME_LIBRARY = "/usr/lib/*/faketime/libfaketime.so.1"


def clock_env(clock: str) -> dict[str, str]:
    """Environment that starts the agent's clock at `clock` ("YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS", UTC) and lets it run forward.

    The conversations happen on their own dates, not the host's, so an agent that reads the time (datetime.now(),
    date.today()) sees the conversation's. Needs libfaketime, which the image installs; on Linux without it the
    run stops rather than give the agent the wrong date. Elsewhere (local tests on macOS) the host clock stays.
    """
    if not clock:
        return {}
    found = sorted(glob.glob(FAKETIME_LIBRARY))
    if not found:
        if sys.platform == "linux":
            raise RuntimeError(f"libfaketime not found at {FAKETIME_LIBRARY}: cannot set the agent's clock")
        return {}
    return {"LD_PRELOAD": found[0], "FAKETIME": f"@{clock}", "FAKETIME_DONT_FAKE_MONOTONIC": "1", "TZ": "UTC"}


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Sandbox:
    """How the agent process runs: as `user` when the host is root, with `limits` on its resources, importing the
    kit from `kit_path`, its clock starting at `clock` (empty: the host's). Errors of a `passthrough` type mean the
    run itself failed and propagate."""

    user: pwd.struct_passwd | None = None
    limits: bool = True
    kit_path: str = KIT_PATH
    passthrough: tuple[type[BaseException], ...] = ()
    clock: str = ""


class AgentProcess:
    """The subprocess running redwood_kit.candidate from a frozen workspace.

    `serve` answers each call the agent makes (`model`, `embed`, `billing`, `developer`) with the reply
    body; an exception becomes an `ok: false` reply the agent sees, except the sandbox's passthrough types.
    """

    def __init__(self, workspace: Path, log: Path, home: Path, serve: Serve, sandbox: Sandbox) -> None:
        self.serve = serve
        self.passthrough = sandbox.passthrough
        self.position = 0  # set by the session: the position of the current request in the conversation
        self.log = log.open("a")
        user = sandbox.user
        start = f"import sys; sys.path.insert(0, {sandbox.kit_path!r}); from redwood_kit.candidate import main; main()"
        self.process = subprocess.Popen(
            [sys.executable, "-I", "-B", "-c", (LIMITS if sandbox.limits else "") + start],
            cwd=workspace,
            env={"HOME": str(home), "TMPDIR": str(home), "LANG": "C.UTF-8", "PATH": "/usr/local/bin:/usr/bin:/bin",
                 **THREADS, **clock_env(sandbox.clock)},
            stdin=subprocess.PIPE, stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=self.log,
            text=True, bufsize=1, start_new_session=True,
            user=user.pw_uid if user else None, group=user.pw_gid if user else None,
            extra_groups=() if user else None,
        )

    def close(self) -> None:
        with contextlib.suppress(ProcessLookupError, PermissionError):  # macOS: EPERM for an exited group
            os.killpg(self.process.pid, signal.SIGKILL)
        self.process.wait(timeout=10)
        self.log.close()

    def _write(self, payload: JsonObject) -> None:
        assert self.process.stdin is not None
        self.process.stdin.write(json.dumps(payload) + "\n")
        self.process.stdin.flush()

    def _read(self) -> JsonObject:
        timer = threading.Timer(CALL_TIMEOUT, lambda: os.killpg(self.process.pid, signal.SIGKILL))
        timer.start()
        try:
            assert self.process.stdout is not None
            line = self.process.stdout.readline()
        finally:
            timer.cancel()
        if not line:
            raise RuntimeError("candidate process exited or timed out")
        return _JSON_OBJECT.validate_json(line)

    def request(self, payload: JsonObject) -> JsonObject:
        """Send one request and serve the agent's calls until its reply arrives."""
        self._write(payload)
        while (reply := self._read()).get("call"):
            try:
                self._write({"ok": True, **self.serve(reply)})
            except self.passthrough:
                raise  # not the agent's doing: the run is invalid
            except Exception as error:
                self._write({"ok": False, "error": str(error)[:2000]})
        if not reply.get("ok"):
            raise RuntimeError(f"candidate error: {reply.get('error')}")
        return reply


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- the conversation


def _stopped(message: Message) -> bool:
    return isinstance(message, UserMessage) and any(token in (message.content or "") for token in STOP_TOKENS)


_CUSTOMER_ENDINGS = (
    (TRANSFER_TOKEN, Termination.CUSTOMER_TRANSFER),
    (OUT_OF_SCOPE_TOKEN, Termination.CUSTOMER_OUT_OF_SCOPE),
)


def _customer_termination(message: Message) -> Termination:
    text = "" if isinstance(message, MultiToolMessage) else message.content or ""
    return next((ending for token, ending in _CUSTOMER_ENDINGS if token in text), Termination.CUSTOMER_STOP)


def _tool_message(item: JsonObject) -> ToolMessage:
    message = from_dict(item)
    if not isinstance(message, ToolMessage):
        raise TypeError("expected a tool message")
    return message


class Session:
    """One conversation: greeting, agent turns with tool rounds, and the developer's replies.

    A subclass supplies the agent process (`start`), the models it may call, and whether the
    conversation has been handed to a team. `run` ends when the developer sends a stop token, the
    agent stops itself, or the conversation hits `MAX_STEPS`; an error of a `passthrough` type
    propagates (an invalid run), any other becomes `agent_error`.
    """

    passthrough: tuple[type[BaseException], ...] = ()

    def __init__(self, customer: Speaker) -> None:
        self.customer = customer
        self.max_steps = MAX_STEPS
        self.messages: list[Message] = [AssistantMessage(content=GREETING)]
        self.agent: AgentProcess | None = None
        self.termination = Termination.AGENT_ERROR
        self.reply: str | None = None  # the agent's last text reply
        self.error: str | None = None

    # ---- supplied by a subclass

    def start(self) -> AgentProcess:
        raise NotImplementedError

    def models(self) -> tuple[tuple[ModelConfig, ...], tuple[ModelConfig, ...]]:
        """(agent models, embedding models) the agent is told it may call."""
        raise NotImplementedError

    def handed_off(self) -> bool:
        raise NotImplementedError

    # ---- the loop

    def run(self) -> None:
        try:
            self._converse()
        except self.passthrough:
            raise
        except Exception as error:
            self.termination = Termination.AGENT_ERROR
            self.error = f"{type(error).__name__}: {error}"[:4000]

    def _converse(self) -> None:
        pending = self._open()
        steps = 0
        while not _stopped(pending):
            if steps == self.max_steps:
                self.termination = Termination.MAX_STEPS
                return
            steps += 1
            customer_message = self._turn(pending)
            if customer_message is None:
                return  # the agent stopped itself
            pending = customer_message
        self.termination = _customer_termination(pending)

    def _open(self) -> Message:
        self.agent = self.start()
        models, embedding_models = self.models()
        self.agent.request({"op": "init", "models": [asdict(m) for m in models],
                            "embedding_models": [asdict(m) for m in embedding_models],
                            "first_message": to_dict(self.messages[0])})
        pending = self.customer.reply(GREETING, handed_off=False)
        self.messages.append(pending)
        return pending

    def _turn(self, pending: Message) -> Message | None:
        """One agent turn plus any tool rounds; returns the next developer message, or None on agent stop."""
        agent = self._agent()
        agent.position = len(self.messages)
        turn = TurnReply.model_validate(agent.request({"op": "turn", "message": to_dict(pending)}))
        reply = from_dict(turn.message)
        self.messages.append(reply)
        if not isinstance(reply, AssistantMessage) or reply.has_text_content() == reply.is_tool_call():
            raise RuntimeError("agent returned a message that is neither text nor tool calls")
        next_pending = self._run_tool_calls(reply) if reply.is_tool_call() else None
        if not reply.is_tool_call():
            self.reply = reply.content
        if turn.stop:  # after any tool calls on the closing message have run
            self.termination = Termination.AGENT_STOP
            return None
        if next_pending is not None:
            return next_pending
        answer = self.customer.reply(reply.content or "", handed_off=self.handed_off())
        self.messages.append(answer)
        return answer

    def _run_tool_calls(self, reply: AssistantMessage) -> Message:
        agent = self._agent()
        agent.position = len(self.messages)
        outputs = ToolsReply.model_validate(
            agent.request({"op": "tools", "tool_calls": [asdict(c) for c in reply.tool_calls or []]}))
        tool_messages = [_tool_message(item) for item in outputs.tool_messages]
        self.messages.extend(tool_messages)
        return tool_messages[0] if len(tool_messages) == 1 else MultiToolMessage(tool_messages)

    def _agent(self) -> AgentProcess:
        if self.agent is None:
            raise RuntimeError("conversation has no agent process")
        return self.agent

"""The simulated developer: a fixed script, optionally worded by a model.

The developer writes the script's opening, then one agenda message per agent reply, whatever the
agent said. It answers `ask_developer` from the script's facts and `confirm_with_developer` with the
script's fixed answer, and logs both. Once the conversation has been handed to a team it ends with a
transfer (the console is closed by then); otherwise it ends with a stop when the agenda is used up.

`WrittenCustomer` has a model word each opening and agenda line as a reply to what support just
wrote. Code still decides everything else: which line is said on which turn, the facts, the consent
answer and the ending. The model never sees the facts, so it cannot answer a question asked in chat:
the developer answers only through `ask_developer`. A wording that drops a number or identifier, or
fails, is replaced by the scripted line itself.

Grading and practice conversations both use this module, so a practice developer behaves like a
graded one.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import re
from collections.abc import Callable
from typing import Literal, Protocol

from pydantic import BaseModel, ConfigDict, model_validator

from .developer import FIELDS
from .jsontypes import Json, JsonObject
from .messages import UserMessage

TRANSFER_TOKEN = "###TRANSFER###"
OUT_OF_SCOPE_TOKEN = "###OUT-OF-SCOPE###"
STOP_TOKENS = ("###STOP###", TRANSFER_TOKEN, OUT_OF_SCOPE_TOKEN)
UNKNOWN_FACT = "I don't have that."
DECLINE_REPLY = "No, please don't do that."
APPROVE_REPLY = "Yes, go ahead."
STOP_MESSAGE = "Thanks, that's what I needed. ###STOP###"
# Fields that name the same fact: asking for either gets the developer's answer to whichever the script has.
SAME_FACT = {"invoice_month": "billing_period", "billing_period": "invoice_month"}
TRANSFER_MESSAGE = "Thanks for passing it on. ###TRANSFER###"


class CustomerScript(BaseModel):
    """The scripted developer: what they write, in order, and what they answer when asked.

        opening   the first message, after the agent's greeting
        agenda    the next messages, one per agent reply, whatever the agent said
        facts     answers to `ask_developer`, by field; any other field gets "I don't have that"
        confirm   the answer to every `confirm_with_developer`; `confirm_reply` is said with it

    Once the conversation is handed to a team the developer ends it with a transfer on the agent's next
    reply; otherwise they end it with a stop when the agenda is used up. So every question the agent must
    answer from the console is asked before the handoff the scenario expects.
    """

    model_config = ConfigDict(frozen=True, extra="forbid")

    opening: str
    agenda: tuple[str, ...] = ()
    facts: dict[str, str] = {}
    confirm: Literal["yes", "no"] = "yes"
    confirm_reply: str = ""

    @model_validator(mode="after")
    def _facts_use_the_field_vocabulary(self) -> CustomerScript:
        unknown = sorted(set(self.facts) - set(FIELDS))
        if unknown:
            raise ValueError(f"facts use fields outside redwood_kit.developer.FIELDS: {unknown}")
        return self

    """One `ask_developer` or `confirm_with_developer` call and the developer's answer.

    `order` is how many console calls had run before it, so a write at console log index `i`
    came after this call exactly when `order <= i`.
    """

    model_config = ConfigDict(frozen=True)

    op: str
    order: int
    fields: list[str] = []
    proposal: str = ""
    answer: JsonObject = {}

    """Anything that can play the developer; the scripted `Customer` or a test double."""

    calls: list[DeveloperCall]

    def reply(self, agent_text: str, handed_off: bool) -> UserMessage: ...

    def handle(self, request: JsonObject, order: int) -> JsonObject: ...


class Customer:
    """The developer, played from a `CustomerScript`."""

    def __init__(self, script: CustomerScript) -> None:
        self.script = script
        self.sent = 0  # messages written so far: the opening, then agenda items
        self.calls: list[DeveloperCall] = []

    def reply(self, agent_text: str, handed_off: bool) -> UserMessage:
        """The next message: the opening, the next agenda item, or the ending."""
        del agent_text  # the script does not depend on what the agent wrote
        if handed_off:
            return UserMessage(content=TRANSFER_MESSAGE)
        messages = (self.script.opening, *self.script.agenda)
        if self.sent < len(messages):
            self.sent += 1
            return UserMessage(content=messages[self.sent - 1])
        return UserMessage(content=STOP_MESSAGE)

    def handle(self, request: JsonObject, order: int) -> JsonObject:
        """Answer one developer call from the agent's tools."""
        match request.get("op"):
            case "ask":
                return self._ask(request.get("fields"), order)
            case "confirm":
                return self._confirm(request.get("proposal"), order)
            case other:
                raise ValueError(f"unknown developer op {other!r}")

    def _ask(self, fields: Json, order: int) -> JsonObject:
        if not isinstance(fields, list) or not all(isinstance(f, str) and f in FIELDS for f in fields):
            raise ValueError(f"fields must be a list drawn from {list(FIELDS)}")
        names = [f for f in fields if isinstance(f, str)]
        facts = self.script.facts
        answers: JsonObject = {name: facts.get(name) or facts.get(SAME_FACT.get(name, ""), UNKNOWN_FACT)
                               for name in names}
        self.calls.append(DeveloperCall(op="ask", order=order, fields=names, answer={"answers": answers}))
        return {"answers": answers}

    def _confirm(self, proposal: Json, order: int) -> JsonObject:
        if not isinstance(proposal, str) or not proposal.strip():
            raise ValueError("proposal must say what you will do")
        default = APPROVE_REPLY if self.script.confirm == "yes" else DECLINE_REPLY
        answer: JsonObject = {"answer": self.script.confirm, "message": self.script.confirm_reply or default}
        self.calls.append(DeveloperCall(op="confirm", order=order, proposal=proposal, answer=answer))
        return answer


RULES = """You are the developer who contacted Redwood Inference billing support. \
Write the way this person writes: {persona}

YOUR MESSAGE THIS TURN must say everything in this line, in your own words, as a reply to support's last message. \
Keep every number, ID, date, time, amount and name in it exactly as written. Leave nothing out and add no new request:
"{line}"

Rules:
- You answer support's questions only through their form, never in chat. If support's last message asks you a \
question in chat, don't answer it and don't say you lack the answer; just say your line.
- If support's last message asks you to approve or confirm an action, also give this answer to it: "{approval}"
- If support repeats something you said earlier in a different way that changes its meaning, correct it.
- Don't mention team names, priority codes or how the ticket should be filed, and don't guess Redwood's policies.
- Write one to four sentences. Reply with only your message."""

# Identifiers with a digit (invoices, requests, lines) and numbers: a wording must keep every one of them.
KEEP = re.compile(r"[A-Za-z]+[-_][\w-]*\d[\w-]*|\d[\d,.:]*\d|\d")

# (instructions, conversation so far) -> the model's text, or None. Raising counts as a failed call.
Complete = Callable[[str, str], "str | None"]


def instructions(persona: str, line: str, approval: str) -> str:
    """The wording model's instructions for one line."""
    return RULES.format(persona=persona or "a developer", line=line, approval=approval)


def keeps_every_value(line: str, written: str, org: str = "") -> bool:
    """The wording still carries every number and identifier the scripted line had, and the org if it named it."""
    plain = written.lower().replace(",", "")
    values = [*KEEP.findall(line), *([org] if org and org in line else [])]
    return all(value.lower().replace(",", "") in plain for value in values)


class WrittenCustomer(Customer):
    """The script, each opening and agenda line worded by a model in the developer's words."""

    def __init__(self, script: CustomerScript, persona: str, complete: Complete | None = None) -> None:
        super().__init__(script)
        self.persona, self.complete = persona, complete
        self.transcript: list[str] = []

    def reply(self, agent_text: str, handed_off: bool) -> UserMessage:
        scripted = super().reply(agent_text, handed_off)
        self.transcript.append(f"Support: {agent_text}")
        line = scripted.content or ""
        if any(token in line for token in STOP_TOKENS):  # endings stay exactly as scripted
            return scripted
        written = self._write(line)
        self.transcript.append(f"You: {written}")
        return UserMessage(content=written)

    def _approval(self) -> str:
        # The same answer confirm_with_developer gives; consent still counts only through that tool.
        return self.script.confirm_reply or (APPROVE_REPLY if self.script.confirm == "yes" else DECLINE_REPLY)

    def _instructions(self, line: str) -> str:
        return instructions(self.persona, line, self._approval())

    def _model_text(self, line: str, instructions: str, conversation: str) -> str | None:
        """The wording model's raw answer for `line`; a subclass may send the parts instead of the instructions."""
        del line
        if self.complete is None:
            raise RuntimeError("no wording model")
        return self.complete(instructions, conversation)

    def _reword(self, line: str, instructions: str, conversation: str) -> str:
        """The model's wording of `line`, or the line itself when the call fails or drops a value."""
        try:
            text = " ".join((self._model_text(line, instructions, conversation) or "").split())
        except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001 - any model fault falls back to the scripted line
            return line
        org = self.script.facts.get("org_id", "")
        return text if text and "###" not in text and keeps_every_value(line, text, org) else line

    def _wording(self, line: str, instructions: str, conversation: str) -> str:
        """Where a subclass can cache wordings; by default every line is worded afresh."""
        return self._reword(line, instructions, conversation)

    def _write(self, line: str) -> str:
        written = self._wording(line, self._instructions(line), "\n".join(self.transcript))
        self.calls.append(DeveloperCall(op="say", order=-1, proposal=line,
                                        answer={"message": written, "fallback": written == line}))
        return written
"""Practice conversations: run your workspace through the same conversation loop graded conversations use.

    python -m redwood_kit.practice SCRIPTS.json [--case ID ...] [--workspace /app/workspace] [--out DIR]

    developer  your script's facts and consent answer (`redwood_kit.customer.Customer`)

transfer after a handoff or a stop when the agenda is used up.

/app/framework/client_api/practice_conversations.json.

        return self._reword(line, instructions, conversation)

    def _write(self, line: str) -> str:
        written = self._wording(line, self._instructions(line), "\n".join(self.transcript))
        self.calls.append(DeveloperCall(op="say", order=-1, proposal=line,

import time
from pathlib import Path

import lancedb
import pyarrow as pa

sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).parent))
from corpus import chunk_records  # noqa: E402

from redwood_kit.embeddings import embed

MODEL = "sentence-transformers/all-MiniLM-L6-v2"
DENSE_THRESHOLD = 2.5
WORKSPACE = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
INDEX = WORKSPACE / "index"
CACHE = Path("/tmp/redwood-vector-cache.json")


def main(root: Path) -> None:
    started = time.time()
    chunks = chunk_records(root)
    dense = [c for c in chunks if c["billing_score"] >= DENSE_THRESHOLD]
    lexical = [c for c in chunks if c["billing_score"] < DENSE_THRESHOLD]
    print(f"{len(chunks)} chunks; dense {len(dense)} ({len({c['source'] for c in dense})} records); "
          f"lexical-only {len(lexical)}")

    cache = json.loads(CACHE.read_text()) if CACHE.exists() else {}
    keys = [hashlib.sha256(c["text"].encode()).hexdigest() for c in dense]
    todo = sorted({k: c["text"] for k, c in zip(keys, dense) if k not in cache}.items())
    if todo:
        print(f"embedding {len(todo)} new chunk texts")
        vectors = embed(model=MODEL, inputs=[t for _, t in todo])
        cache.update({k: v for (k, _), v in zip(todo, vectors)})
        CACHE.write_text(json.dumps(cache))
    for key, chunk in zip(keys, dense):
        chunk["vector"] = cache[key]

    db = lancedb.connect(str(INDEX))
    for name, rows, with_vectors in (("billing", dense, True), ("corpus", lexical, False)):
        fields = [pa.field("id", pa.string()), pa.field("text", pa.string()), pa.field("source", pa.string()),
                  pa.field("platform", pa.string()), pa.field("title", pa.string()),
                  pa.field("status", pa.string()), pa.field("date", pa.string()), pa.field("labels", pa.string()),
                  pa.field("part", pa.int32()), pa.field("record_hash", pa.string()),
                  pa.field("billing_score", pa.float64())]
        if with_vectors:
            fields.append(pa.field("vector", pa.list_(pa.float32(), 384)))
        schema = pa.schema(fields)
        data = [{f.name: r[f.name] for f in fields} for r in rows]
        table = db.create_table(name, data=pa.Table.from_pylist(data, schema=schema), mode="overwrite")
        table.create_fts_index("text", replace=True, with_position=True)
        print(f"table {name}: {table.count_rows()} rows")
    manifest = {
        "embedding_model": MODEL,
        "dense_threshold": DENSE_THRESHOLD,
        "built_at": time.strftime("%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S"),
        "records": {c["source"]: c["record_hash"] for c in chunks},
        "dense_records": sorted({c["source"] for c in dense}),
    }
    (INDEX / "manifest.json").write_text(json.dumps(manifest, indent=0))
    print(f"done in {time.time() - started:.0f}s")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main(Path(sys.argv[1] if len(sys.argv) > 1 else "/app/R"))
